patch.summary: Changes part of one recipe and returns it as it now stands.
patch.description:
This is a JSON Merge Patch, not a replacement. A field the body does not mention is left exactly as
it is; a field sent with a value is set to it; a field sent as `null` is cleared. Omitting a field
never blanks it. `tags` is the one field that replaces rather than merges — a submitted list becomes
the recipe's complete set, and `[]` or `null` removes them all. `title` and `status` may be changed
but not cleared. `expectedConcurrencyToken` is required and is not a field of the recipe: it is the
`concurrencyToken` from the read this edit was composed against, and an edit quoting a token the
recipe has moved past is refused with `409 recipes.recipe.conflict` rather than overwriting whoever
saved first. `reason` is likewise not a recipe field; it is recorded on the version this edit writes.
An edit that would change nothing writes no version and leaves the token valid. The response is the
whole recipe, in the same shape a read returns, so an editor can rebind from it: it carries the
refreshed token the next edit must quote, and the version this one wrote.

a change to an old one. Metadata only — a version's content is never returned here, however many
versions a recipe has. Cursor-paged: follow `nextCursor` until it is null. A cursor is bound to the
workspace and recipe it was issued for, so replaying one against another recipe is refused with
`recipes.cursor.invalid_request` rather than silently paging the wrong history. `limit` is clamped
rather than refused. There is no total; follow the pages to count them. There is no `sort` — newest
first is the contract. An unknown recipe and another workspace's recipe both answer
`404 recipes.recipe.not_found`. A recipe created through this API has a version 1, so its history is
normally non-empty — but an empty page is a legitimate answer and a client must render it rather than
read `items[0]` unguarded.

get.summary: Compares two of one recipe's versions and returns what differs between them.
get.description:
Read-only, and it writes nothing: comparing two versions leaves no record that it happened. The
comparison is calculated on the server from the two archived documents and is the only one — a client
renders it rather than deriving a second diff of its own, which is why the two snapshots are not
returned. `from` and `to` are version numbers as the history lists them, not version ids: a number is
unique only within its recipe, so a number naming another recipe's version matches nothing rather than
being refused by a check. Either order is allowed, and `from` equal to `to` answers a comparison with
no changes in it. An unknown recipe and another workspace's recipe both answer
`404 recipes.recipe.not_found`; a version number this recipe does not have answers
`404 recipes.version.not_found`, naming the parameter at fault. Section order is fixed and every
section is present whether or not it changed, so a client renders a stable frame. Positions are ranks
among siblings, not stored sort orders, and a reorder is reported as a move rather than as a
replacement.

post.summary: Shelves one recipe: archives it without deleting anything.
post.description:
**Archiving is not deleting.** Every version, tag, media link, ingredient line and step stays exactly
where it was, and the recipe is still readable by id — its history, its version comparisons and
copying it all keep working. What changes is that it drops out of the default library listing
(`GET .../recipes` returns it only for `?status=Archived`) and stops accepting content changes:
`PATCH` and version restore both answer `409 recipes.archived.conflict` until it is brought back, and
the AI proposal, publishing and test-run seams will do the same when they exist. Requires the Editor
role, because archiving takes a recipe out of every collaborator's library rather than contributing to
one. `expectedConcurrencyToken` is required: archiving a recipe someone else is editing should tell
the archiver it moved under them rather than silently shelving work they have not seen. Archiving an
already-archived recipe succeeds and changes nothing — no audit entry, no new token — so the command
is safe to retry and takes no idempotency key. No version is written; the move is recorded in the
audit log instead, because a version records what a recipe *said* and this changes none of that.

post.summary: Brings one recipe back from the archive.
post.description:
The mirror of the archive command, at the same Editor bar and with the same shape. **The recipe comes
back as a `Draft`**, whatever it was before it was shelved — nothing records the earlier state, and
`Ready` is a claim about a finished recipe that a creator picking one back up should make again
themselves. Unarchiving a recipe that is not archived succeeds and changes nothing. Named
`unarchive` rather than `restore` deliberately: `.../versions/{n}/restore` already means putting a
recipe's *content* back, and one word for two operations would be a trap in a client and in this
codebase alike.

post.summary: Copies one recipe into a new, independent recipe of its own.
post.description:
The copy is a recipe in its own right, not a derivative: editing either recipe does nothing to the
other, and the copy has its own history starting at version 1, whose `source` is `Duplicate` and whose
recipe records `duplicatedFromVersionId`. Requires the Contributor role — the same bar as creating a
recipe, and deliberately not the Editor bar a restore carries, because copying takes nothing away from
anyone. `sourceVersionNumber` is optional: omitting it copies the recipe as it currently stands, and a
number is a version number as the history lists it rather than a version id. `title` is required, so a
copy is never momentarily indistinguishable from its source; nothing else may be sent, and editing the
copy afterwards is an ordinary `PATCH`. **The copy is always a `Draft`**, whatever the source's status
— including when the source was archived. Everything the archive holds is copied, including
ingredients, method, equipment, tags and media links, with fresh ids throughout; media links point at
the same assets, and no asset is copied or re-owned. The source's version history, its concurrency
token, its authorship and its timestamps are not copied. There is **no `expectedConcurrencyToken` and
no `409`** — nothing is being overwritten, which makes this the one recipe write with no state to quote.
An unknown recipe and another workspace's recipe both answer `404 recipes.recipe.not_found`; a version
number the source does not have answers `404 recipes.version.not_found`, naming `sourceVersionNumber`.

post.summary: Puts one recipe back to what one of its versions said, as a new current version.
post.description:
Restoring never rewrites history. The version named here is read and left exactly where it is — it does
not become current again, is not renumbered and is not deleted — and the recipe's content is put back as
a *new* version whose parent is the version it replaced and whose `restoredFromVersionId` names the one
it came from. Requires the Editor role, a step above editing, because one request discards every change
made since the chosen version without naming them. `expectedConcurrencyToken` is required and is the
`concurrencyToken` from the read this restore was decided against; one the recipe has moved past is
refused with `409 recipes.recipe.conflict` rather than overwriting whoever saved in between, and nothing
of the creator's is lost by reloading and asking again. `reason` is not a recipe field; it is recorded
on the version this writes. The whole recipe is restored — its own fields including `status`, so
restoring a version captured before a recipe was archived un-archives it, along with its ingredients,
method, equipment, media links and tags. A restore that would change nothing writes no version and
leaves the token valid, so a resubmission is safe. An unknown recipe and another workspace's recipe both
answer `404 recipes.recipe.not_found`; a version number this recipe does not have answers
`404 recipes.version.not_found`, naming `versionNumber`. The response is the whole recipe, in the same
shape a read returns, carrying the refreshed token the next write must quote.

post.summary: Attaches one library asset to the test.
post.description:
Contributor and above, the bar recording a test carries. **This is not an edit of the recipe or of what the
test recorded**: no recipe version is written, and the test's own `concurrencyToken` stays valid.

`versionNumber` **pins the attachment to one version of the asset**, which is usually what evidence of a
trial wants; leave it out to follow whichever is current. `testIssueId` ties the picture to one issue of
this same test. The new attachment goes to the end.

**Only an asset in this workspace's library can be attached.** An unknown asset, another workspace's, and
one removed from the library all answer `422 recipes.testAttachment.target.unprocessable` naming
`mediaAssetId`, in the same words. The same code names `versionNumber` for a version the asset does not
have and `testIssueId` for an issue that is not this test's.

The same asset against the same issue (or against the test as a whole) twice answers
`409 recipes.testAttachment.duplicate.conflict`. Two attachments saved at the same instant can collide on
position: the loser answers `409 recipes.testAttachment.conflict` with nothing written, and should simply
be sent again. An archived recipe answers `409 recipes.archived.conflict`. **Nothing about the asset
changes**, and its usage history is not touched.

get.summary: Lists one recipe's recorded tests, most recently cooked first.
get.description:
Summaries, never the tests themselves: a row carries counts where the test has observations and issues, and
**no attachment byte, asset id or recipe snapshot is read** — `attachmentCount` is the most this route can
say about photographs it cannot yet authorize. `summaryNotes` is the one prose field a row carries;
`environmentNotes` and `equipmentNotes` are not. Cursor-paged: follow `nextCursor` until it is null rather
than comparing counts against a page size the server may have clamped. A cursor is bound to the workspace,
recipe and filters it was issued for, so changing any of them means starting again without one —
`recipes.cursor.invalid_request` says so explicitly. `limit` is clamped rather than refused. `summary`
counts every match across all pages, breaks the verdicts down with every outcome named even at zero, and is
present unless `includeSummary=false`; it describes the **filtered** set, so narrowing the filters narrows
it, and it is **never a readiness verdict** — that is a separate deterministic evaluation. Multi-valued
filters are comma-separated. `version` names version numbers, as the recipe's history lists them, because a
test is always evidence about one exact version. `testedBy` takes the membership ids this route publishes.
There is no `sort`: most recently *cooked* first is the contract, and a test recorded a week late still
belongs to the day it was cooked. An unknown recipe and another workspace's recipe both answer
`404 recipes.recipe.not_found`; a recipe nobody has tested answers an empty page, which a client must
render rather than read `items[0]` unguarded. Every member including a Viewer may read this.

the Contributor role, the same bar as creating a recipe — recording a test adds the creator's own
material and changes no canonical content. **Nothing here writes to the recipe**: every `actual` figure

being overwritten, which makes this one of the two recipe-area writes with no state to quote. The body
carries **no attachments**: linking media needs something that can authorize an asset against this
workspace, and that arrives with the media library. An unknown recipe and another workspace's recipe
both answer `404 recipes.recipe.not_found`; a version number the recipe does not have answers
`404 recipes.version.not_found`, naming `sourceVersionNumber`; an archived recipe answers
`409 recipes.archived.conflict`, and the remedy is to bring it back rather than to retry. A `testedAt`
in the future is refused — testers record the past. Issues point at this request's own observations by
position through `observationIndex`, and the response returns both sets of ids in submitted order so a
client can resolve an issue later without listing the test back.

every issue with its severity, and the resolution on each issue that has one. It also returns

to a previous write. A recipe the caller may not see answers `404 recipes.recipe.not_found`, whether it is
unknown or another workspace's; a test id that is not one of that recipe's answers
`404 recipes.testRun.not_found`. An **archived recipe still answers**: archiving withdraws a recipe from
content changes, not from its own history, so the create and the edit refuse where this does not. Every
member including a Viewer may read this; deciding an issue is closed is what needs an Editor. No tester
display name — the membership ids here are the ones the history publishes beside the names.

A JSON Merge Patch, not a replacement: a field the body does not mention is left exactly as it is, a
field sent with a value is set to it, and a field sent as `null` is cleared. `observations` and `issues`
are the two fields that **replace** rather than merge — a submitted list becomes the test's complete set,

omitted is removed, and `[]` clears them. **There is no `sourceVersionNumber`**: a test is evidence about
the version that was cooked, and repointing it would be a claim that something else happened. An issue
pointing at an observation by `observationIndex` may only do so when `observations` is sent in the same
request, because the positions mean that list. **An issue that has been resolved cannot be dropped** by
omitting it — `409 recipes.testIssue.removal.conflict` — because a resolution records a decision and
removing the issue would erase it. `expectedConcurrencyToken` is required and is the `concurrencyToken`
from the read this edit was composed against; one the test has moved past is refused with
`409 recipes.testRun.conflict` rather than overwriting whoever saved first. **Nothing here writes to the
recipe.** An unknown test, another workspace's, and one belonging to a different recipe all answer
`404 recipes.testRun.not_found`; an archived recipe answers `409 recipes.archived.conflict`. The response
is the whole test, carrying the refreshed token the next edit must quote.

A separate command from the edit above, and deliberately so. It writes exactly one row and **rewrites
neither the issue nor the observation it came from** — the read that judges it does not even track them.
Requires the Editor role, a step above recording a test: reporting a problem and deciding it is closed
are different acts, and this decision is immutable once written. There is **no
`expectedConcurrencyToken`** because nothing is being overwritten; the conflict this route has instead is

is a version number of **this recipe** — the database enforces that, not only this seam — and must be
**later than the version that was tested**, because a version written before the problem was found cannot
contain its fix; naming an earlier one needs `predatingVersionOverrideReason` to say why, which is then
recorded. Only a `Fixed` resolution may name a version at all. An unknown test or issue answers
`404`, and a version this recipe does not have answers `404 recipes.version.not_found` naming the field.

post.summary: Reads one reference image and composes a prompt from what it shows.
post.description:
Contributor or above, the bar for spending the workspace's allowance. `202` rather than `201`: nothing
is read yet, and the model is called by the worker afterwards (api-contract.md). The `Location` header
points at the status resource to poll.

**The image is named, not uploaded here.** It is a picture this workspace already holds, and `source`
says which kind: `BrandDocument` with `referenceDocumentId`, `DamAsset` with `mediaAssetId` (and
optionally `mediaAssetVersionNumber`), or `GeneratedImage` with `generatedImageId`. Send exactly one
source and only that source's ids; anything else is a `400` naming the field. A body carrying only
`referenceDocumentId`, with no `source`, is a `BrandDocument` — the shape this route took before it
accepted the other two.

JPEG, PNG, WEBP and GIF are readable. A picture that is anything else, one too large to send, one this
workspace does not have, a removed asset, a version the asset does not have, a declined or expired
generated image, and one that does not exist all answer `404 ai.referenceImage.not_found` — one answer
for every source, because each is a client naming something it was not shown.

**The version is pinned when the request is made.** The bytes the model reads are the ones named,
even if the document or the asset is replaced in the minutes before the worker claims the operation.
An asset named without a version is pinned to its current one.

**A reading of a library asset or a generated image may be kept with that picture**, so that later
work on it need not look twice. Only what was observed is kept — never the prompt — and only for a
request with no note, about a picture with a single frame.

**The image is untrusted material, and so is the note.** Both are sent as material to describe rather
than as instructions. Writing photographed into the image is described as part of what the picture
shows; it is not obeyed.

**What the answer will not contain.** No identification of a person, no claim about who owns a brand,
a product or the photograph, and no statement about the food's safety, nutrition, allergens or dietary
suitability — each is refused rather than returned. Every observation carries its own confidence
(`Clear`, `Probable`, `Unclear`), because a confident misreading of someone's reference is worse than
an uncertain one. An animated GIF is read as its opening frame, with a warning saying so.

**Nothing is rendered and no recipe changes.** The answer is observations plus one prompt and a list
of things to avoid; it proposes no recipe edit, and the creator's edit of the prompt is what becomes
authoritative when they save it to their library.

get.summary: Returns the workspace's weekly themes.
get.description:
The creator's own editorial week — at most one theme per day, so at most seven, and fewer is normal. These
are not a platform list: a creator writes their own, nothing is seeded, and no two workspaces share a
theme.

The live week comes first in a creator's reading order, Monday through Sunday, followed by retired themes.
A retired theme is reported rather than hidden, with `retiredAt` set, because its `key` may already be
stored by other records and because a client may offer to bring it back. A workspace with no themes
answers `200` with an empty list, not `404`: an empty week is where every workspace starts, and a consumer
reading it simply has no theme for the day. Every member including a Viewer may read. The response is
`no-store`: it is workspace-private and editable.

parameters.name: workspaceSlug
parameters.description:
Bound only so the route is well formed. The workspace is resolved server-side from this segment and the
caller's membership before the action runs, and nothing here reads it (tenancy.md).

default.description: Problem details with a stable `code` and `traceId`.

put.description:
Editor or above. One write for the whole week rather than per-theme CRUD: at most seven day-keyed entries
make the week a single value, which keeps the write idempotent, lets a creator clear a day by leaving it
out, and keeps "one theme per day" an invariant of one transaction instead of a race between endpoints.

A theme is recognised by its `key`, which is stable and is what other records store. Submitting a key the
workspace already has keeps that theme — its `day`, `displayName`, `description` and `standingNotes` are
updated, and it is brought back if it was retired. Submitting a new key creates a theme at `revision` 1. A live theme whose
key is *absent* is retired, not deleted: its row and its key survive, so a record that already named it
keeps resolving, and its day is freed. A request asking for the week the workspace already has writes
nothing and bumps no revision.

`standingNotes` is optional free text the creator writes for the day — "always under 30 minutes, never
tofu" — of at most 2000 characters. It is stored as written, trimmed at the ends, and is never written or
rewritten by a model. Like `description`, omitting it or sending it blank clears it, and changing it alone
bumps that theme's `revision`. A retired theme keeps its notes.

`displayName` is the creator's own words and the server does not police them. `key` must be lowercase and
match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; each `day` and each `key` may appear once. Two creators saving at the same
time is last-write-wins by design — the week is one value, so there is no field-level merge to lose — and
a genuine collision between two concurrent replaces answers `409 content.weekly_themes.conflict`. A
workspace already holding the maximum number of rows, retired ones included, answers
`422 content.weekly_themes.limit.unprocessable`; the remedy is to delete a retired theme.

get.summary: Returns what the workspace has already made for one themed day.
get.description:
The pieces of work carrying this theme's `key` that came to something: a picture the creator saved to the
library and kept for the work (`KeptPicture`), posts they accepted (`AcceptedPosts`), or a recipe the work
names that they made by accepting an AI first draft (`AcceptedRecipeDraft`). Work that came to nothing is
not listed. Newest outcome first.

The history is derived from records of what the creator did. It is not stored as history, cannot be
written to, and has no route that changes it. Each item carries the work's `contextId`, the creator's own
`workingTitle` for it, and the ids of what it came to — never a post body, recipe text or a picture. An
accepted post that has since been marked for review stays listed with `needsReview` set: the acceptance
still happened. An archived piece of work stays listed with `isArchived` set.

Bounded: outcomes from the last 365 days, drawn from the 200 most recently touched pieces of work for the
theme, at most 50 items in all. `limit` is 1 to 25 and defaults to 10; out-of-range values are clamped.
Loop until `nextCursor` is null. A cursor is bound to the workspace and the theme it was issued for, and
one from anywhere else answers `400 content.weekly_theme.history.cursor.invalid`.

A retired theme's history reads exactly as it did before it was retired. A key this workspace does not
have answers `404 content.weekly_theme.not_found` — as does a deleted theme's and another workspace's, so
one workspace's themes are never disclosed to another. Every member including a Viewer may read. The
response is `no-store`.

Owner only, and audited. This is not how a creator clears a day — leaving a theme out of `PUT` retires it,
which is reversible and keeps its key resolving for anything that stored it. This deletes the row, so the
key resolves to nothing afterwards and a record that stored it keeps only the creator's text. It exists for
a theme written by mistake, and because the retired tail is what the per-workspace row limit counts.

The response is the remaining week, exactly as a read returns it. A key this workspace does not have
answers `404 content.weekly_theme.not_found` — as does another workspace's key, so one workspace's themes
are never disclosed to another. Creating a theme under a deleted key again later is allowed, and it then
resolves again, to whatever the creator has written under it now.

get.summary: Lists every guided workflow, and whether the caller can start it now.
get.description:
Every member including a Viewer may read. One entry per workflow, at its newest version, in the order the
product offers them: `goal`, `description` and `expectedOutcome` are plain language for the creator.

**Whether a start would be accepted, asked in advance.** `canStart` is true when the workflow is built
(`available`), nothing it needs first is missing (`waitingFor` is empty), and the caller can take its first
step — a Contributor at least, and whatever more that step needs. When the caller's role is the only thing in
the way, `neededRole` names the least role that could. Each `waitingFor` entry says what is missing in plain
words and, in `route`, the page relative to the workspace where it is sorted out (`brand`, `recipes`), or null.
A workflow not built yet has `available` false and its `unavailableReason`.

`startsFrom` names the kinds of record a workflow can begin from elsewhere in the product; starting from none
is always allowed. The answer is the same for every member of a role, holds no workspace record, and is
`no-store` because whether a prerequisite is met is this workspace's.

get.summary: Lists the workspace's runs, a page at a time.
get.description:
Every member including a Viewer may read.

**Views.** `mine` (the default) is the runs in progress the reader started or that are assigned to them;
`completed` is the workspace's completed runs; `attention` is the workspace's runs in progress that need a
look; `all` is every run in the workspace, whatever its state. `definition` narrows any view to one workflow
by key; a key no workflow has is an empty page. A view or filter that cannot be read answers
`400 workflows.run.list.invalid`.

**Order.** Most recently changed first, and for `attention` the longest-waiting first. Two runs changed at the
same moment are ordered by id, which is what keeps a page boundary from repeating one and skipping the other.
The list is not a snapshot: a run that changes while you page moves to its new place, so it can be missed by
the pages still to come or met twice. Start again from the first page for a fresh look.

**Needs attention**, decided from each run alone — `attentionReasons` says which applies, on every run in
progress whatever the view: `idle` when no one has touched it for seven days; `newer_version` when a newer
version of its workflow has shipped since it started; and `not_yours_to_do` when the step it is on needs more
access than the reader has. Treat the codes as an open set. A record a run holds that has gone is not checked
here; the run page warns of it.

**Each row is a summary**: the run's own state, counts and dates; its workflow's `goal`; its `owner` and
`assignee` by membership, with `displayName` null for someone who has left; the step it is on (or was left on);
`linkedResource` — the record it started from, or else the last one it made — by kind and id only; and
`nextAction`, the step's main action and whether the reader can take it, while it is in progress and has a step
to do. No row carries a draft, a reason the creator gave, an address, or anything a linked record holds: the
run page has those.

**Paging is by keyset cursor.** Pass a page's `nextCursor` back as `cursor`; it is null on the last page. A
cursor is bound to the workspace, the view, the filter and the reader it was issued for, and one replayed
against another answers `400 workflows.run.list.cursor.invalid` rather than a page from the wrong list.
`limit` outside 1–100 is clamped, not refused. The response is `no-store`.

post.summary: Starts a run of one guided workflow.
post.description:
Contributor or above; a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`, and a workspace the caller is
not in — or that does not exist — answers `404`. The run starts on the newest version of the workflow and
belongs to the caller. It records where the creator is and does nothing else: the first step's work is not
done for them, and no record is made in place of one that is missing.

**The name.** Leave `title` out to use the workflow's goal; one sent blank is a `400`, and one sent is
trimmed.

**Starting from a record.** The record is checked through the module that owns it. One this workspace does
not have answers `422 workflows.run.starting_resource.unprocessable` — the same answer another workspace's
gets. A kind the workflow does not start from is a `400`. When the first step's whole job is to link a
record of that kind, and another step remains, the run starts with that step done.

**Refusals.** A workflow that cannot be taken yet answers `422 workflows.definition.unavailable.unprocessable`
with its `reason`. A caller who cannot take the first action, nor any alternative to it, answers
`403 workflows.run.role_insufficient.forbidden` naming the `neededRole`. Something the workflow needs
before it starts answers `422 workflows.run.prerequisites_unmet.unprocessable` with `waitingFor`.

**The answer** is the run, every step's state, its links, and `nextAction`: the step to do now, its
actions with their workspace-relative `route`s, and anything it is still `waitingFor`. `Location` is the
run's own address.

parameters.name: workspaceSlug

caller's membership before the action runs (tenancy.md).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Required. For 24 hours, a repeat of the same key and the same request returns the run the first one started,
as it stood then, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different request answers
`422 idempotency.key_reused`. A name that differs only by surrounding spaces is the same request. After the
window the key starts a new run. A missing key answers `400 idempotency.key_required` and a malformed one
`400 idempotency.key_invalid`.

get.summary: Reads one run: where it stands, and how to carry on.
get.description:
Every member including a Viewer may read every run in the workspace. Reading changes nothing — no date, no
step, no `concurrencyToken`.

**The version it started on.** A run is shown against the version of its workflow it was started on, never
a newer one. While it is in progress and a newer one exists, `warnings` says so with `newer_version`; the run
carries on as it began.

**Carrying on.** `nextAction` is the step the run is on, its actions as the *reader* can take them
(`youCanDoIt` uses the reader's role, so a Viewer's is always false), and anything it is still
`waitingFor`. Once every step is done the run waits on its last one for finishing, and `nextAction` is null. `resumeRoute` is where "Continue" goes: where the creator last was, unless that names a record
that is gone; else the first of the next step's actions that exists and has an address. Both are null once
the run is completed or abandoned, and `resumeRoute` is null when the next step needs a record the run no
longer holds.

**Warnings** do not stop the run: `link_missing` for a record the run holds that can no longer be found —
gone or never this workspace's, which read alike, and with no title; `draft_missing` for a step's saved draft
that has gone the same way; `newer_version`; and
`next_step_needs_role` when the reader cannot take the next action. Treat the codes as an open set and
show `message` for one you do not know.

An unknown run and another workspace's run both answer `404 workflows.run.not_found`. A `runId` that is not
a GUID matches no route and answers the router's own `404 not_found`.

put.summary: Points the run's current step at the record its unfinished work is kept in.
put.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**A pointer, never the work.** Each step's work is saved by the screen it happens on, in a record that
screen's module owns; this keeps only where to find it. The kinds a step takes are its actions' draft kinds —
a kind it does not take is a `400`, and a record this workspace does not have answers
`422 workflows.step.draft.unprocessable`, the same answer another workspace's gets.

**Safe to repeat.** Saving the pointer the step already holds writes nothing and answers `200` with the
token unchanged — whatever the token sent, and even once the run has moved on or finished — so a debounced
client or a retry after a timeout always lands; no `Idempotency-Key` is needed. A token is still required on
every save, and a missing or malformed one is a `400`. **Never over a newer edit:** any other change must send the token last read, and one sent against a
run that has since changed answers `409 workflows.run.conflict` carrying `currentConcurrencyToken` and the
draft the step holds now. Nothing is written then. A stale token is answered before the record is looked at,
so it is a `409` whether or not the record exists.

The first draft starts the step. The answer is the run as stored after the save — `draftSavedAt` on the
step is the "Saved just now" — and is sent only once the save is committed.

A finished run answers `409 workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`; a step that is not the current one,
`409 workflows.step.not_current.conflict` with `currentStepKey`; the run's last step once it is done,
`409 workflows.step.already_done.conflict`; a step the run's version does not have,
`404 workflows.step.not_found`; an unknown run and another workspace's, `404 workflows.run.not_found`.

post.summary: Saves where the creator is on the run's current step, so they can leave and carry on later.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**Leaving is not a status.** The run stays `InProgress` on the step it is on: nothing is completed, skipped
or abandoned, and no step moves. `updatedAt` is when it was saved.

**The draft.** Send `draft` when the step's last draft may not have reached the run — an autosave still on
its way. It follows the draft save's rules exactly: a kind the step does not take is a `400`, and a record this
workspace does not have answers `422 workflows.step.draft.unprocessable`, the same answer another workspace's
gets. Leave it out to keep the draft the step holds; a save and exit never clears one.

**Where to carry on.** Send `capabilityKey` — one of the step's actions, as `nextAction` lists them — and the
server stores the route that action opens for this run, filled from the run's own records, as `lastRoute`.
No address is taken from the client. `resumeRoute` then leads back there until the run moves to another step:
completing, skipping or going back clears it. An action this step does not offer is a `400`; one not built
yet, or whose page needs a record the run does not hold, answers `422 workflows.run.last_route.unprocessable`.
Leave it out to keep the route the run holds.

**Safe to repeat.** A save and exit whose draft and route the run already holds writes nothing and answers
`200` as the run stands, whatever the token — and so does a duplicate that loses a race to the first. No
`Idempotency-Key` is needed. A token is still required on every call, and a missing or malformed one is a
`400`. Any other must send the token last read; a stale one answers `409 workflows.run.conflict` carrying
`currentConcurrencyToken`, the draft the step holds now and the run's `lastRoute`, and nothing is written.

**Which answer wins**, when more than one applies: a malformed request (`400`), the run (`404`), who may change
it (`403`), the step (`404`), a finished run (`409`), a step that is not current (`409`), an action the step
does not offer (`400`), an action with no page (`422`), nothing to change (`200`), a step already done or
passed over (`409`), a draft of the wrong kind (`400`), a stale token (`409`), and a draft not found (`422`).

The answer is the run as stored after the save, sent only once it is committed. Codes:
`workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`, `workflows.step.not_current.conflict` (with `currentStepKey`),
`workflows.step.already_done.conflict`, `workflows.step.not_found`, `workflows.run.not_found` — the same for
an unknown run and another workspace's.

post.summary: Completes the run's current step, once the server finds it done.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above, as for a draft.

**Not a claim — a question.** The server checks the step's own rule against the modules that own the work: a
fresh readiness evaluation, the recipe's or the piece's state as stored, whether the guide is switched on,
whether a post was kept, the publishing ledger's own state (an outcome still uncertain never counts). Nothing
here changes any of those, so no step completes that the domain would not already call done. When the rule is
not met the answer is `422 workflows.step.incomplete.unprocessable` with `missing` — what stands in the way,
in plain words — and nothing is written.

**Results.** A step whose job is to make a record — start a recipe, keep a picture, file a piece — is done when
it names that record: in `results`, or, left out, by the step's saved draft, or else by the record of that
kind the run already holds (so a step reopened by Back completes again on what it made the first time). Each is checked first: one this
workspace does not have answers `422 workflows.step.result.unprocessable`, the same answer another workspace's
gets (and says so when it was the draft's), and a kind the step does not make is a `400`. Naming a record the
run already holds makes it the run's latest of its kind again.

**What it moves, together:** the step is completed, its results are linked to the run (once each), the run's
progress counts it, the run moves on to the next step not yet done or passed over, and its `lastRoute` is
cleared so "Continue" goes there. On the last one the run
waits on the last step of its version and `nextAction` is null; finishing the run is a separate command. `readyToComplete` is true
as soon as every *required* step is done — an optional step may still be open, and `nextAction` then offers
it. The answer is the run as stored after the save.

**Safe to repeat.** A step already complete answers `200` as the run stands, with nothing written, whatever
results are sent and however far the run has moved since — and so does a duplicate that loses a race to the
first. The request must still be well formed: a token is required on every call, and a missing or malformed
one is a `400`. Any other completion must send the token last read; a stale one answers
`409 workflows.run.conflict` with `currentConcurrencyToken`.

**Which answer wins**, when more than one applies: the run (`404`), who may change it (`403`), the step
(`404`), a step already complete (`200`), a finished run, a step that is not current, a step passed over (each
`409` — the last is `workflows.step.already_done.conflict`, and Back reopens it), a result of the wrong kind
(`400`), a stale token (`409`), a result not found (`422`), and the rule not met (`422`).

A finished run answers `409 workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`; a step that is not the current one,
`409 workflows.step.not_current.conflict` with `currentStepKey`; a step the run's version does not have,
`404 workflows.step.not_found`; an unknown run and another workspace's, `404 workflows.run.not_found`.

post.summary: Goes back from the run's current step to the one before it, reopening that step.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**Back reopens the step before.** The run moves to the step immediately before `stepKey` in its version, and
that step becomes open again: a completed step's completion, or a skipped step's skip, is cleared and taken
off the run's counts, so it can be worked on and completed again — through the ordinary completion, which
checks its rule afresh. Nothing goes forward this way, and no step after the current one is touched.

**Nothing is lost.** The step being left keeps its state and its saved draft; the reopened step keeps its
draft; no record the run holds is unlinked. `lastRoute` is cleared, so "Continue" goes to the reopened step
rather than the page just left.

**Safe to repeat.** Because `stepKey` names the step being left, a Back whose result already holds — the run
is on the step before `stepKey`, and that step is open — answers `200` as the run stands with nothing written,
whatever the token. That is so whether this Back put the run there or a request named a later step than the
run had reached; either way it is where the Back would leave it. The one exception is a run finished since,
which answers as a finished run. Any other Back must send the token last read; a stale one answers
`409 workflows.run.conflict`. A token is required on every call, and a missing or malformed one is a `400`.

**Which answer wins**, when more than one applies: a malformed request (`400`), the run (`404`), who may change
it (`403`), the step (`404`), a finished run (`409`), a Back whose result already holds (`200`), a step that
is not current (`409`), the first step (`409`), and a stale token (`409`).

Back from the first step answers `409 workflows.run.at_first_step.conflict`; from a step that is not the
current one, `409 workflows.step.not_current.conflict` with `currentStepKey`; on a finished run,
`409 workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`; a step the run's version does not have,
`404 workflows.step.not_found`; an unknown run and another workspace's, `404 workflows.run.not_found`.

post.summary: Passes over the run's current step, which its workflow must mark optional.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**Optional steps only.** A step its workflow requires answers `422 workflows.step.required.unprocessable`.

**A skip is never a result.** The step is marked passed over — when, by whom, and why if the creator said —
and nothing more: no record is linked, nothing is completed, the step's saved draft stays a draft, and the run's
completed count is untouched. The run moves on to the next step not yet done or passed over, or, with none,
waits on its last step to be finished; its `lastRoute` is cleared, as for a completion. Back undoes a skip.

**Safe to repeat.** A step already skipped answers `200` as the run stands with nothing written, whatever was
sent and however far the run has moved since; so does a duplicate that loses a race to the first. A token is
still required on every call, and a missing or malformed one — or a blank or over-long `reason` — is a `400`.

**Which answer wins**, when more than one applies: a malformed request (`400`), the run (`404`), who may change
it (`403`), the step (`404`), a step already skipped (`200`), a finished run, a step that is not current, a
step already done (each `409`), a required step (`422`), and a stale token (`409 workflows.run.conflict` with
`currentConcurrencyToken`). Codes: `workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`,
`workflows.step.not_current.conflict` (with `currentStepKey`), `workflows.step.already_done.conflict`,
`workflows.step.not_found`, `workflows.run.not_found` — the same for an unknown run and another workspace's.

post.summary: Finishes a run, once the server finds every required step done as things stand now.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**Proved now, not remembered.** Every step the run's version requires must be completed, and its rule must
still hold when this is asked: a record a step linked is checked again through the module that owns it, and
every other rule — readiness, the recipe's or the piece's state, the guide switched on, a post kept, the
publishing ledger — is evaluated afresh. A step completed on a recipe since un-approved, or a picture since
deleted, is not done. When anything stands in the way the answer is
`422 workflows.run.incomplete.unprocessable` with `incompleteSteps` — each step's `stepKey`, `title` and
`missing`, in plain words — and nothing is written. Optional steps never stand in the way.

**The run, and only the run.** The run becomes `Completed` with `completedAt`, and is on no step any more;
`nextAction` and `resumeRoute` are null. No step, link or linked record is touched: an optional step left open
stays open with its draft, and the recipe, piece or picture the run used is exactly as it was. The answer is the
run as stored after the save.

**Safe to repeat.** A run already completed answers `200` as it stands with nothing written, whatever the
token — and so does a duplicate that loses a race to the first. A token is still required on every call, and a
missing or malformed one is a `400`. Any other must send the token last read; a stale one answers
`409 workflows.run.conflict` with `currentConcurrencyToken`.

**Which answer wins**, when more than one applies: a malformed request (`400`), the run (`404`), who may change
it (`403`), a run already completed (`200`), a run stopped (`409 workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`), a
stale token (`409`), and something still to do (`422`). An unknown run and another workspace's answer
`404 workflows.run.not_found` alike.

post.summary: Stops a run for good, keeping it whole and every record it linked as it is.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**Confirmed, or nothing happens.** `confirmed` must be `true`; without it the answer is
`400 workflows.run.abandon.invalid` and nothing changes. `reason` is optional, in the creator's own words, up to
500 characters; it is kept trimmed and returned as `abandonReason`. Leave it out rather than send it blank: a
blank or over-long one is a `400`, as for a skip.

**A stop, not a finish.** The run becomes `Abandoned` with `abandonedAt`; `nextAction` and `resumeRoute` are
null. Nothing else in it changes: it keeps the step it was left on, its steps with their drafts and reasons, and
every link, as the record of how far it got. No recipe, piece of content or picture it linked is touched, and
the stop is recorded in the workspace's audit log in the same write. To try the journey again, start it over or
start a new run.

**Safe to repeat.** A run already stopped — this way or by a start over — answers `200` as it stands with
nothing written, whatever the token, and keeps the reason it was first stopped with; so does a duplicate that
loses a race to the first. A token is still required on every call, and a missing or malformed one is a `400`.
Any other must send the token last read; a stale one answers `409 workflows.run.conflict` with
`currentConcurrencyToken`.

**Which answer wins**, when more than one applies: a malformed or unconfirmed request (`400`), the run (`404`),
who may change it (`403`), a run already stopped (`200`), a run completed
(`409 workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`), and a stale token (`409`). An unknown run and another
workspace's answer `404 workflows.run.not_found` alike.

post.summary: Starts a run over: stops it, keeping it whole as history, and starts the same journey afresh.
post.description:
The run's owner, the person it is for, or an Editor and above; anyone else answers
`403 workflows.run.forbidden`, and a Viewer is refused by the route with `403 forbidden`.

**Confirmed, or nothing happens.** `confirmed` must be `true`; without it the answer is
`400 workflows.run.restart.invalid` and nothing changes. Edits the creator has not saved live only in their
browser, so they should be saved before this is asked.

**Not a reset.** The old run is stopped — `Abandoned`, with `replacedByRunId` naming the new one — and kept whole:
its steps, their reasons and drafts, and every record it linked stay as they were. No recipe, piece of content
or picture is touched by either run.

**The new run** starts as a start does, on the newest version of the same workflow. It keeps the old run's
owner and the person it is for, and its name unless `title` is sent; and the record the old run started from,
when the workflow still starts from that kind and the record is still there. The answer is `201` with the new
run and its `Location`.

**Never a third run.** A run already started over answers `200` with the run that replaced it, whatever key is
sent and whichever token — though one must still be sent, and well formed. A finished run otherwise answers `409 workflows.run.not_in_progress.conflict`; a stale token,
`409 workflows.run.conflict`; a caller who cannot take the new run's first action,
`403 workflows.run.role_insufficient.forbidden`; an unknown run and another workspace's,
`404 workflows.run.not_found`.

get.description:
Any member may read. Each item is an `id` to send and a `name` to show — the id is what a recipe's or a
library asset's `tags` field takes.

**Active tags only.** A retired tag stays named on whatever already carries it, through that record's
own read, and is simply not offered here. A workspace with no tags yet answers an empty list, never a
`404`.

**Not paged, and capped at 500.** A picker filters the whole vocabulary as a creator types, and a
workspace's own tags are a small set; past the cap the list is cut alphabetically rather than growing
without limit. Ordered by name, case-insensitively.

**Read-only.** A tag enters the vocabulary when a creator tags a recipe. The response is `no-store`:
the vocabulary is the creator's own words.

post.summary: Captures one piece of the caller's own work in the workspace named by the route.
post.description:
Contributor and above; a Viewer is refused with `403`. **`title` is the
only required field** — everything else is optional, and everything the request does not carry the
server decides: the owner is the caller, the assignee is the owner, the status is always `Backlog`,
and the task goes to the bottom of its list. The place is not published; the order a list arrives in
is the order.

**A capture lands in the week you are planning in.** With no `planningWeekStart`, the week holding
`scheduledDate` is used; with neither, the week holding today in the workspace's scheduling zone. A
week is named by its first day and **starts on a Monday**; any other day answers `400`. A day outside
its week answers `400` too. A workspace that has set no scheduling zone gets a task in no week rather
than one guessed for it — capture never fails for want of a setting.

**An estimate and labels may come with a capture** (13A.31): `estimateMinutes` from 1 to 1440, and
`labelIds` — at most 25, each named once — which must each be an active tag of this workspace, or the
answer is `422 planning.work_task.label.unprocessable`, the same whether a tag never existed, was
retired or is another workspace's. The task and its labels are one write. **A due date, a status, an
assignee and a recurrence are not part of capturing**: those are the server's or a later edit's, and
sending one is ignored rather than honoured.

**Every linked record must be this workspace's own.** `recipeId`, `contentCardId`, `mediaAssetId` and
`workflowRunId` are each checked through the record's owner before anything is written, and
`workflowStepKey` must be a step of the run beside it. One that cannot be linked answers
`422 planning.work_task.link.unprocessable` naming the field — **the same answer whether the record
never existed, can no longer be used, or belongs to another workspace**, so a task cannot be used to
ask what a neighbour owns. A step key with no run is a `400`.

**Nothing is half-written.** `409 planning.work_task.conflict` means the write did not happen and the
request is safe to send again as it stands.

With an `Idempotency-Key`, a repeat of the same request returns the first answer with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` and creates nothing more; the same key with a different body is refused.
Without a key, two identical requests are two tasks.

Answers `201` with the task. **There is no `Location`**: a task has no read route of its own yet.
The response is `no-store` — it is one person's private working list.

patch.summary: Edits one of the caller's own tasks. Only what the patch mentions changes.
patch.description:
Contributor and above, and only **the task's owner or the person doing it**: anyone else's task, an
unknown one and another workspace's all answer the same `404 planning.work_task.not_found`.

**A field left out is untouched; a field sent with a value is set; a field sent as `null` is cleared.**
`title`, `priority` and `assigneeMembershipId` can be changed but not cleared. A `description` sent
blank is cleared. `labelIds` is the whole set and replaces what the task carries; `null` or `[]`
clears it.

**An edit does not move, reorder or complete a task.** Sending `status` or `position` answers `400`
naming it.

**Days and weeks.** A `scheduledDate` sent alone brings its week with it. Clearing the day keeps the
week, so the task joins that week's backlog. **A day is never dropped as a side effect**: changing
`planningWeekStart` while the task keeps a day outside the new week answers `400` unless
`scheduledDate` is sent in the same patch — a day in the new week, or `null`.

**Links.** `recipeId`, `contentCardId`, `mediaAssetId`, `workflowRunId` and `workflowStepKey` can each
be set, replaced or cleared, and none is unlinked unless its field is sent as `null`. Changing the run
while the task names one of its steps answers `400` unless `workflowStepKey` is sent too. A newly
linked record is checked exactly as on capture, and one that cannot be linked answers
`422 planning.work_task.link.unprocessable` — the same whether it never existed, can no longer be used,
or belongs to another workspace. A record the task already points at is not checked again. An edit
never changes a linked record.

**Labels** are the workspace's own tags. A newly added one must be an active tag of this workspace, or
the answer is `422 planning.work_task.label.unprocessable`; one the task already carries stays after it
is retired.

**Handing a task on.** The owner may hand it to any active member who can keep work — Contributor and
above — themselves included. The person doing it may hand it back to the owner and to nobody else.
Anything else answers `422 planning.work_task.assignee.unprocessable`. A task handed on, or planned for
another day, goes to the bottom of its new list.

`expectedConcurrencyToken` is required. When the task has changed since that read the answer is
`409 planning.work_task.stale.conflict` and **nothing is written** — keep what was typed, read the task
again, and send again. A token that could never have been issued is a `400`. A patch that changes
nothing writes nothing and returns the same token.

Answers `200` with the task, its labels and its new `concurrencyToken`. The response is `no-store`.

post.summary: Moves one of the caller's own tasks to another of their lists, at a place in it.
post.description:
Contributor and above, and only **the person doing the task** — a move rearranges their list, and not even
the owner who handed it on rearranges someone else's. Anyone else's task, an unknown one and another
workspace's all answer the same `404 planning.work_task.not_found`.

**The lists are the planner's.** `status` is required. `Backlog` with a `scheduledDate` is that day's
list, and the week follows the day. `Backlog` without one is the backlog of no day: in
`planningWeekStart` when sent, in the week the task already has when not. `InProgress` and `Waiting` are
one list each and **keep the task's day and week** — a task started on Monday is still Monday's — so
sending a day or week with them answers `400`; changing the plan is an edit. `Done` is not a list a task
is moved to: complete it. A finished task answers `409 planning.work_task.completed.conflict`: reopen it.
A day and a week that disagree answer `400`.

**A move is a change of list.** Naming the list the task is already in answers `400`: reorder it within
its list instead.

**Its place.** `beforeTaskId` names the task it goes immediately before, which must be in the target
list; left out, it goes to the bottom. One that is not answers `422 planning.work_task.move.unprocessable`
— the same whether that task does not exist, is in another list, is the task being moved, or is somebody
else's. The order is deterministic: rank, then id.

**The move is one write.** When two neighbours have no room between them the target list is re-spaced in
its own order, in the same write; no other list is touched, though re-spacing can change the
`concurrencyToken` of other tasks in that list, never what they say.

`expectedConcurrencyToken` is required. `409 planning.work_task.stale.conflict` means the task — or a task
that had to be re-spaced to make room — changed first, and **nothing was written**: read the list again
and move it again. A token that could never have been issued is a `400`.

A move changes only the task: it completes no workflow step and touches no linked record. Answers `200`
with the task and its new `concurrencyToken`. The response is `no-store`.

Optional. For 24 hours, a repeat of the same key and the same request returns the first answer with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` and moves nothing more; the same key with a different request answers
`422 idempotency.key_reused`. Without a key a repeat cannot move twice either: it quotes a token the first

post.description:
Contributor and above, and only **the person doing the task**: anyone else's task — the owner who handed it
on included — an unknown one and another workspace's all answer the same `404 planning.work_task.not_found`.

**Only its place changes**: never its status, day, week, links or labels. Its list is the one it is in —
in progress, waiting, the not-started tasks of its day, or the not-started tasks of no day.

`beforeTaskId` names the task it goes immediately before, which must be in the same list; left out, it goes
to the bottom. The task itself, or one not in its list, answers `422 planning.work_task.move.unprocessable`
— the same whatever that task turns out to be. The order is deterministic: rank, then id. When two
neighbours have no room between them the list is re-spaced in its own order in the same write, which can
change other tasks' `concurrencyToken` in that list, never what they say; no other list is touched.

**A task already exactly there is left alone** and keeps its token. A finished task answers
`409 planning.work_task.completed.conflict`: finished tasks read in the order they were finished.

`expectedConcurrencyToken` is required. `409 planning.work_task.stale.conflict` means the task, or a task
that had to be re-spaced, changed first, and **nothing was written**. A token that could never have been
issued is a `400`. Answers `200` with the task and its `concurrencyToken`. The response is `no-store`.

post.summary: Finishes one of the caller's own tasks.
post.description:
Contributor and above, and only **the person doing the task**: anyone else's task — the owner who handed it
on included — an unknown one and another workspace's all answer the same `404 planning.work_task.not_found`.

The task becomes `Done` and records when, by whom, and the status it was finished from. **Its day, week and
place in its list are kept**, so reopening puts it back exactly where it stood. A task already finished
answers `409 planning.work_task.completed.conflict`.

**Nothing else finishes with it.** A workflow step the task is about is done only when the workflow's own
rule is satisfied; no linked record is touched.

`expectedConcurrencyToken` is required: `409 planning.work_task.stale.conflict` means the task changed first
and nothing was written; a token that could never have been issued is a `400`. Answers `200` with the task
and its new `concurrencyToken`. The response is `no-store`.

parameters.description: Bound only so the route is well formed; see the capture route.

parameters.description: The task to finish.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Optional. For 24 hours, a repeat of the same key and the same request returns the first answer with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` and changes nothing more; the same key with a different request answers
`422 idempotency.key_reused`. Without a key a repeat cannot take effect twice either: it quotes a token the
first used, and answers `409`.

post.summary: Takes one of the caller's finished tasks up again, where it stood.
post.description:
Contributor and above, and only **the person doing the task**; anyone else's, an unknown one and another
workspace's answer the same `404 planning.work_task.not_found`.

The task goes back to **the status it was finished from**, on the day and week and in the place it had, and
its record of when and by whom it was finished is cleared. A task that is not finished answers
`409 planning.work_task.open.conflict`. A workflow step the task is about is not reopened with it.

`expectedConcurrencyToken` is required, as for completing. Answers `200` with the task and its new
`concurrencyToken`. The response is `no-store`.

get.summary: What "Add to my plan" would make for one workflow step. Writes nothing.
get.description:
Contributor and above. Every field is a suggestion to show the creator before anything exists: the step's
own title, a line naming the run, **no estimate** — a step carries none and an unknown is never offered as
a number — no day, and the week holding today in the workspace's zone (none when no zone is set).
`workflowRunRoute` is the run's address, relative to the workspace. `existingTask` is the task the caller
already added for this step, when they have, so the screen can say so instead of offering it twice.

A run this workspace does not have, or a step not in it, answers `422 planning.work_task.link.unprocessable`
— one answer for a run that never existed and another workspace's. A run no longer in progress, or a step
already done or passed over, answers `422 planning.work_task.step.unprocessable`: there is nothing left to
plan. The response is `no-store`.

post.summary: "Add to my plan": makes the caller's task for one workflow step, or answers with the one they have.
post.description:
Contributor and above. **The task is made only here, on confirmation, for the one step named** — never for
every step of a run. Only `workflowRunId` and `workflowStepKey` are required; anything left out takes the
suggestion, so confirming it unchanged is one click. A `description` sent blank is none.

**One task per person per step.** `201` with `created: true` when this request made it; `200` with
`created: false` and the task the caller already added for this step. The store keeps it so, whatever
arrives at once. A task pointed at the same step by hand is not that task and does not count.

**The run is read, never written.** The task points at the run and step, and its `links.workflowRunRoute`
leads back there; the run gains nothing and no step changes state. Finishing the task does not finish the
step. Refusals are the suggestion route's. The response is `no-store`.

parameters.description:
Optional. For 24 hours, a repeat of the same key and the same request returns the first answer — the same
status and `created` — with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different request answers
`422 idempotency.key_reused`. Without a key a repeat still makes nothing more: it answers with the task
already there.

get.summary: Reads the caller's own day in the workspace named by the route.
get.description:
Every member including a Viewer may read, because what comes back is **the caller's own work and
nobody else's**: every group is keyed on the caller's membership as the task's assignee, so another
member's list is not something this route can be asked for. A task handed to the caller appears here
even though someone else captured it, and names that person as its `owner`.

**The groups do not overlap.** A task is placed by the first rule it matches: `completedToday`, then
`overdue`, then `inProgress`, then `waiting`, then `scheduledToday`. So the day is not double-counted,
and ticking one thing off does not make it disappear from two places. The precedence hides nothing —
every row carries its own `status`, `dueDate` and `scheduledDate`, so a task in `overdue` still says
it is in progress. A task finished on an earlier day is in none of them.

**`date` and `timeZoneId` say what "today" meant**, and are always present, so a client never infers
the day boundary. The zone is the workspace's own, from brand settings. `completedToday` is a range of
instants — local midnight to the next, the end exclusive — so a day that springs forward is 23 hours
long and nothing is counted twice across a fall-back. `scheduledDate` and `dueDate` are plain dates
and are compared as written.

**A workspace that has set no time zone answers `422 planning.today.time_zone_not_set.unprocessable`**
rather than guessing a day boundary, because a guessed one does not fail visibly: it quietly files an
evening's work under tomorrow. The remedy is brand settings, and the message says so.

Each group holds at most 50, newest or most pressing first, with `...HasMore` true when there were
others. There is no cursor: a day is bounded by what a person can do, and a group past 50 is a sign of
something other than a plan.

`suggested` is empty unless `includeSuggestions=true`. It offers at most three **unplanned** backlog
tasks — never one already in a group above — each with a plain-language `reason`. **Offering one
schedules nothing**: no day, no status, no place in the list is written by this route, which is a
`GET` and writes nothing at all.

`topThree` names the tasks the caller chose as today's top three (13A.32), by id and in order — each is
still in its own group, and only one shown in a group is named. Empty until they choose; see
`PUT top-three`.

An unknown workspace and another workspace's answer the same `404`. The response is `no-store`: it is
one person's private working list.

parameters.name: workspaceSlug
parameters.description: Bound only so the route is well formed; see the capture route.

parameters.name: includeSuggestions
parameters.description: Ask for a few unplanned tasks worth a look. Off unless sent.

put.summary: Chooses the caller's top three for today in the workspace named by the route.
put.description:
Contributor and above. **The whole set, replacing the last**: at most three `taskIds`, each once, first the one
that matters most; an empty list clears the choice. A repeat writes what is already there, so there is no
idempotency key. More than three, one named twice, or a missing list is a `400 planning.top_three.invalid`.

**Only a task on the caller's day may be chosen**: theirs to do, and late, planned for today, in progress,
waiting or finished today — exactly what `GET today` shows them. Anything else answers
`422 planning.top_three.unprocessable`, **the same whether the task is planned for another day, somebody
else's, another workspace's, or was never a task.**

**Choosing changes no task**: no status, day, priority or place in a list. The choice is kept for today in the
workspace's own zone, so tomorrow starts with none; a workspace with no zone set answers
`422 planning.today.time_zone_not_set.unprocessable`. `GET today` returns it as `topThree`.

`409 planning.top_three.conflict` means nothing was written and the request is safe to send again. Answers
`200` with the day and the ids as they now stand. The response is `no-store`.

get.summary: Reads the caller's own week in the workspace named by the route.
get.description:
Every member including a Viewer may read, because what comes back is **the caller's own work and
nobody else's**: every group is keyed on the caller's membership as the task's assignee.

**A week runs Monday to Sunday, everywhere.** `weekStart` is written `yyyy-MM-dd` and must be a Monday;
any other day or format answers `400 planning.week.invalid`. The caller's language does not move the
week. Left out, it is the week holding today in the workspace's own zone. `weekStart`, `weekEnd`,
`today` and `timeZoneId` are always present, so a client never infers a boundary, and `isCurrentWeek`
says whether this is the week holding today.

**The groups do not overlap, and none is a content-board column.** `completed` is what was finished
between this Monday's local midnight and the next, the end exclusive — so a week the clocks spring
forward in is 167 hours long and nothing is counted twice across a fall-back. `inProgress` and
`waiting` are the caller's now, whatever week they were planned for. Each of the seven `days` holds the
not-started tasks planned for that date. `backlog` is planned for the week and no day of it;
`unplanned` is planned for no week at all; `carriedOver` is not started and planned for an earlier
week, oldest first, and only in the current week — empty in any other. A not-started task planned for a
later week is in none of them.

**Order is the caller's own arrangement**: the place each task was given, then its id, in every group
but `completed`, which is newest first. Unlike `today`, priority does not reorder a week.

**Totals count the whole group**, not the rows returned: `taskCount`, `estimatedTaskCount`, and
`estimatedMinutes` — the sum of the estimates there are. A task with no estimate is never counted as
nothing, so `estimatedMinutes` is null when no task in the group has one. `planned` adds up the seven
days and `backlog`: the week's own work, and nothing nobody planned for it.

Each group, and each day, holds at most 50 rows, with `hasMore` true when its `taskCount` is more.

**A workspace that has set no time zone answers `422 planning.week.time_zone_not_set.unprocessable`**,
even for a week named outright: the week's edges are local midnights, and a guessed zone would quietly
move Sunday evening's work into the next week. The remedy is brand settings.

An unknown workspace and another workspace's answer the same `404`. The response is `no-store`: it is
one person's private working list.
